findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE: A and C are contradictories on one variable — whether slide distance was measured at all. A says he logged how sharply the foot stopped but not how far it slid; C reports both a shorter stop and less slide. B (release method) and D (between-arena vs between-visit variance) sit on other axes, so the pair marks where the key lives.

CROSS_QUESTION: q:3 ('nothing in them to stiffen when the school is cold') and q:5 (two of four options turn on temperature) tell a passage-blind reader that cold is the governing variable of this text; C is the only option here that states a cold effect, so the sibling stems select it.
justification: Blind I can tell the passage is about instrumented readings on a waxed riding surface and that cold is its headline variable, because two later stems say so. That plus the A/C contradiction gets me to about 45 % on C. What I cannot tell blind is whether the passage's actual claim is the cold effect (C) or the measurement-scope caveat (A) — A is exactly the kind of self-imposed limit that q:4 then asks the writer to endorse, which is a live alternative reading. Channel is real but does not settle the key.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: C carries an absolutizer with a causal add-on ('since no hoof ever reaches that deep') — the unit's recurring over-claim tell — and is eliminable on form alone, lifting the rest above base rate.

CROSS_QUESTION: q:3 option C asserts that damp schools 'carry no fibre', which hands a passage-blind reader the fact that the waxed bed under discussion does contain fibre and makes fibre a measured, stratifiable variable; that nudges D over A and B.
justification: I get to roughly 40 % on D: cores are taken to show stratification, one option is eliminable as an over-claim, and a sibling option volunteers that fibre is the material at issue. What I cannot infer blind is which stratification the cores actually showed — wax loss on lower grains (A), grain breakdown against spec (B) and fibre depletion at the bottom (D) are all coherent findings and nothing in the stems discriminates them. The pull is thematic, not propositional.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: the stem names the contrast itself ('damp rather than waxed'), and B is the only option that explains on the wax axis. A runs on bed age, C on fibre, D on reading times — three options answer a question the stem did not ask, which is a free narrowing to one.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: each of A, C and D carries an unsupported add-on or absolutizer ('newer than this one, so they have not begun to settle', 'They carry no fibre', 'the two grids never catch the change'), the same over-claim tell that runs through this unit.
justification: Blind I reach about 48 % on B purely from axis-matching: the stem sets up wax as the variable and only one option's explanation uses it. What I cannot infer is the direction of the claim — whether the passage says a damp school rides constant through the day (B) or that it simply has no wax to stiffen in the cold, in which case C is a right-shape/wrong-substance near-miss built to catch exactly that inference. Real channel, not a reliable route to the key.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: textbook attitude triad. B is the over-credulous extreme ('treats the tie ... as settled by his readings'), C is the over-dismissive extreme ('gives a yard nothing it can act on'), and A is the moderate middle that credits the researcher's own caveats. On this item type the moderate middle is the key by construction.
PAIR_STRUCTURE: B and C are contradictories on the single variable 'does this method establish anything', the standard tell that neither limb is the key.
STUDENT-AVAILABLE: yes, form only. No horses, no biomechanics, no English idiom is needed — a test-wise 18-year-old who knows that attitude keys avoid both poles lands on A.
justification: I would take A at roughly 65-70 % without the passage. The set is built so that the two extremes cancel each other and D ('readier to doubt the riders than his figures') is a partisan stance that an academic-register writer is not going to be handed. Nothing here required me to know what the readings were about. This is answerable blind by form, and the form is the cheapest kind of test-wiseness to teach, so it is a kill rather than a flag.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: C over-claims exclusivity ('are what settle how it rides') and is eliminable without the passage.

CROSS_QUESTION: the four sibling stems read as a table of contents of the passage — readings inside the school, cores from the bed, damp vs waxed schools, the writer's stance on the testing. That pins the subject to surface temperature and maintenance depth and lifts the temperature-centred options (B, C) as a family, giving the main-idea item a floor of roughly 35-40 % on that family rather than 50 % on any one option.
justification: This is the unit's main-idea item and it is the least leaky of the five. I land on B at about 35 % — barely above base rate — because two opposite signals fight: content says temperature is the spine (B, C), while the hedging tell says the key is one of the two modalised options (A 'probably', D 'may'). Since there are two modalised options, the one-modal rule does not fire and the hedging signal is uninformative. I cannot tell blind whether the passage's punchline is the temperature effect or a maintenance-over-temperature twist.

Gap 1 with no passage is a flat guess at 25 %. The only structural observation is a 3+1 shape — Hence, Rather and Equally are logical connectives while Elsewhere is spatial — but Elsewhere is a perfectly ordinary discourse connective in English prose ('Elsewhere, the picture is different'), so the odd-one-out does not disqualify it. Eliminating nothing reliably, I sit at base rate. I picked Rather on no better ground than frequency.

findings: MIRRORED_TWIN: 'cut' and 'break' are near-interchangeable in the agreement register the rest of the cloze establishes (cut/break off, cut/break ties). A test-wise reader who applies the twins-cancel heuristic — if two options mean the same thing neither can be the key — is pushed to a 50/50 between 'join' and 'fall', which lands him squarely on distractors if the key is in fact one of the twins.
justification: I cannot solve this gap: 'break' is my pick at about 28 %, on collocational frequency alone. The flag is not for solvability but for the opposite failure — the twin pair rewards a wrong heuristic. Whether cut and break are genuinely interchangeable here depends on the collocation the passage supplies, which I have not seen; if they are, the item is degenerate, and if they are not, the item punishes a reasonable strategy. Round 2 should check which.

Four near-synonyms from one commercial/agreement field (transaction, negotiation, bargain, settlement) with no odd-one-out and no form tell — this is exactly how a lexical-precision gap should look. I am at about 33 % on 'bargain', and only because gaps 4 and 5 make the passage's theme willingness-to-honour-an-agreement, which favours the noun that takes 'keep one's side of'. Cross-gap thematic coherence is inherent to the cloze format, not a leak, so this is a pass.

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE: clean 2+2 antonym cross — grudging/wholehearted on the willingness axis, outspoken/muted on the expressiveness axis. Binding calibration scores a 2+2 as a channel: it tells a blind reader the key is a pole on one of two named axes, and gap 5's own willingness axis lets him bet which.
GENERATOR TIC: the same 2+2 antonym-cross construction is used again at gap 5, so the unit repeats the structure rather than varying it.
justification: I am at about 32 % on 'grudging' — above base rate only because the 2+2 makes the willingness axis the better bet given the rest of the cloze, and because a text about honouring an agreement minimally pairs 'grudging' with gap 5's 'narrowly'. I cannot pick the pole without the passage; the axis is guessable, the direction is not.

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE: second clean 2+2 in the same cloze — narrowly/generously on breadth of interpretation, dutifully/instinctively on motive. Same channel as gap 4, same limitation: the axis is inferable, the pole is not.
justification: About 32 % on 'narrowly'. The 2+2 plus the shared theme with gap 4 gets me an axis but not a direction; a passage that praises compliance would flip me to 'generously' and nothing in the stems tells me which way the writer leans.

findings: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: a reader who knows that pneumatic-tube haemolysis is produced by the acceleration and deceleration at the ends of the run rather than by transit itself goes straight to D. This is expert domain knowledge, NOT student-available — a Swedish 18-year-old almost certainly lacks it.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: A presupposes an intervention the stem never mentions ('once the loop was slowed down'), and C answers a why-question ('why do blood gases go by tube') that the stem did not ask. Both are eliminable on shape, leaving D as the only option shaped like a finding about the samples themselves.
justification: I reach about 45 % on D, and I have to be honest that most of that comes from outside knowledge rather than from the stem. On form alone I would be near 33 % after discarding A and C. B is the one I cannot rule out blind — 'spotted by its colour before it leaves the ward' is false in the real world (haemolysis shows in plasma after spinning) but a passage-blind student has no way to know that. Single-question unit, so there is no cross-question channel at all, which is a point in its favour.

findings: ENTAILMENT: the stem asks what is *implied*, and D is the only option that is an inference rather than a stated fact — the only one that yokes the two threads the option set names (the boundary quarrel and the railway survey) into a motive. On implication items the key is the option that joins the threads, and here exactly one does.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: C reports what happened after the correspondence, out of frame for a letters passage; B's 'for a generation' is a quantity that would be stated rather than implied; A is a provenance detail at too low an altitude for an implication question. Three eliminable on shape.
justification: This sits just under the kill line — I would take D at roughly 55-57 %, on pure form, with no knowledge of Victorian railway law or hedge-laying required. The channel is fully student-available: read the word 'implied', then take the option that supplies a motive linking the two named things. What I cannot verify blind is whether the passage actually makes that link or whether D is a constructed over-reading and the real key is the flatter A. Round 2 should treat this as a near-kill.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: C and D are two flavours of one gradualist position — go slower, at the ensemble's pace or on the small stage first. Functional twins cancel, leaving A and B, and B characterises the opponents' motives rather than stating a 'hållning', which is what the stem asks for.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (altitude/genre): a debattartikel thesis is a full demand with an owned cost, which is A's exact shape — 'bör gå på varje föreställning på stora scenen, även om spelet binds hårdare vid manus'. The concessive clause is the giveaway that this is the writer's own position rather than a compromise offered to him.
justification: I land on A at about 55 % without the passage, on genre shape alone: one maximal demand, two interchangeable gradualisms, one attack on motives. What I cannot tell blind is whether this writer is in fact a maximalist — a piece that argued for D's pilot year would be an equally normal debattartikel, and the 'även om' concession in A could just as easily be the generator's habit as the writer's stance.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: A, B and C are all complaints and D is the only neutral technical fact. In a piece arguing for surtitles the loop is raised in order to be shown insufficient, and 'nås genom hörapparatens T-läge' is precisely the proposition that makes it insufficient — it serves only those with a T-coil — without asserting a fault the passage would have to document.

CROSS_QUESTION: q:1's option set establishes, before this question is read, that the text is a debattartikel pressing for surtitles in a theatre with two stages and a resistant ensemble. That fixes the rhetorical role of the loop in advance.
justification: About 45 % on D. The genre plus the 3-complaints/1-fact split gives a real pull, but I cannot separate D from B blind — 'fungerar sämre i de bakre raderna' is an equally serviceable premise for the same argument, and a writer who had a specific autumn breakdown to report (A) would report it. The channel gets me a rhetorical role for the loop, not the sentence the passage actually contains.

findings: RULE 15 (a) ONE-WAY LEAK — Q2 into Q1, strong form. Clause by clause: q:2 A ('Den har slutat fungera i höst') hands a q:1-blind reader that the auditorium HAS an induction loop and that it may be failing; q:2 B ('fungerar sämre i de bakre raderna') hands the loop's existence plus partial coverage; q:2 D ('nås genom hörapparatens T-läge') hands its existence plus a coverage limit to T-coil users; only q:2 C ('saknas i programbladet') is orthogonal. The proposition 'the auditorium already has a hearing loop and it is in some way insufficient' therefore survives across three of four options — the strong form, which holds however q:2 resolves. That proposition is the writer's own premise, and it pushes q:1 toward the unconditional demand (A) and away from the two gradualist options (C, D), because a reader who knows the existing accommodation is inadequate reads the writer as impatient rather than incremental.

RULE 15 (a) STEM-BORNE: yes. The q:2 stem alone — 'Vad säger skribenten om hörselslingan i salongen?' — presupposes both that a loop exists and that the writer comments on it. In a debattartikel arguing for surtitles, a writer who stops to discuss the existing loop is discussing it in order to dismiss it. The leak therefore does not depend on reading q:2's options at all; the stem carries it. Running the other way, q:1's options tell a q:2-blind reader that the subject is captioning for the deaf and hard of hearing, which is enough to guess that the loop is raised as insufficient and to demote q:2 C.

RULE 15 (b) SYMMETRIC VOUCHING: yes. Both option sets are drawn from one small factual world — one theatre, one auditorium, a stora and a lilla scen, an ensemble, a surtitle strip, an induction loop, a programme leaflet. Neither set imports an entity the other does not already presuppose, so each vouches for the other's furniture: a reader who doubted that this is a real accessibility argument has that doubt removed twice over.

JOINT STEMS-ONLY SOLVABILITY: q:1 at about 55 % (A) and q:2 at about 45 % (D) give a joint probability near 0.25 against a 0.0625 base rate — roughly four times chance on the pair. Answering either shifts the odds on the other: committing to q:1 A (surtitles on every performance) makes an insufficiency reading of the loop nearly obligatory and demotes q:2 C to near zero; committing to q:2 D (the loop only reaches T-coil users) supplies the premise that a partial remedy is not enough and demotes q:1's gradualist options C and D.
justification: Neither question is individually solvable, but as a pair they are markedly less independent than they should be. The defect is concentrated in the q:2 STEM rather than in its options: naming the hörselslinga at all announces the writer's counter-argument structure, and that announcement is what makes q:1's maximalist option the natural read. The cheapest repair is to make q:2 recoverable only from the passage — for instance by not naming the loop in the stem — or to move the loop question into a unit that does not also ask for the writer's overall stance. What I could not infer as a pair: any of the concrete facts — whether the loop is broken, partial, or merely T-coil-limited, and whether the writer's demand is immediate or staged.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: C is the odd one out on two counts at once — the only option whose subject is 'Hästarna' rather than 'Hovarna', and the only one asserting wholesale replacement. Surface-shape mismatch plus over-claim makes it eliminable blind.

PAIR_STRUCTURE: B and D are contradictories on traction — studs fitted versus hooves slipping on the glare — which marks the pair as where the key lives, while A sits on a different variable (the ice's bearing capacity).
justification: About 38 % on B, so barely above base rate after one free elimination. B is the operationally specific detail a period passage tends to carry, and 'inför de tyngsta lassen' implies the graded, repeated loads that q:2 is about. But I genuinely cannot separate B from D or A blind: hooves breaking through where a person could walk, and hooves slipping on glare ice, are both the sort of concrete image such a text supplies.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: D answers which winters were easier, not how the work was laid out, so it is off the axis the stem names ('hur arbetet lades upp') and is eliminable blind. This is the same off-axis-option tic as las-b22-001 q:4 option D.

PAIR_STRUCTURE: B and D are contradictories on predictability — the days could not be fixed in advance versus sustained cold made the work easier and therefore plannable — leaving a near-flat choice between A and B.
justification: About 35 % on A, essentially a coin flip with B. 'Hushållen turades om och delade på vändorna' answers the stem's question most directly, but 'Vad framgår av texten' invites an inference rather than a stated fact, which argues for B. I cannot resolve that tension without the passage, and I would not be surprised by either.

findings: RULE 15 (a) ONE-WAY LEAK — Q2 into Q1, strong form. Clause by clause: q:2 B ('Det gick inte att bestämma dagarna i förväg') hands a q:1-blind reader that the work is weather-governed; q:2 C ('under en enda lång natt') hands night work in hard frost; q:2 D ('Vintrar med sammanhängande kyla gjorde arbetet lättare') hands that the ice's state is the binding constraint and, by contraposition, that in mild winters the ice fails — which is q:1 option A almost verbatim. The proposition 'the state of the frozen surface, not the crew, is what governs the work' survives across three of four q:2 options and therefore survives non-resolution. Running the other way the leak is weaker but real: q:1 B ('Hovarna fick broddar inför de tyngsta lassen') presupposes graded, repeated loads and advance preparation, which corroborates q:2 A's 'vändorna' while cutting against q:2 B's unplannability and q:2 C's single night.

RULE 15 (a) STEM-BORNE: no. Unlike las-b22-002, neither stem carries the leaking proposition — 'Vad sägs i texten om hästarna?' and 'Vad framgår av texten om hur arbetet lades upp?' are both empty of content. The leak here is entirely option-borne, which makes it cheaper to repair.

RULE 15 (b) SYMMETRIC VOUCHING: yes, and more tightly than in las-b22-002. Both option sets sit in one tiny world — winter, ice and snow, horses and hooves, heavy loads, trips, households, a long night, sustained cold. Every q:1 option is about the hoof-to-ice interface and every q:2 option is about the labour of the same haul, so the two sets confirm each other's entire furniture with no residue. A passage-blind reader can propagate a single reading of the winter across both: commit to a bad-ice winter (q:1 A) and q:2 D becomes the attractive contrast while q:2 B gains; commit to a well-equipped haul (q:1 B) and q:2 A's turn-taking gains while q:2 B loses.

JOINT STEMS-ONLY SOLVABILITY: q:1 at about 38 % (B) and q:2 at about 35 % (A) give a joint probability near 0.13 against a 0.0625 base rate — roughly twice chance. Answering one does shift the odds on the other, materially and in a consistent direction, but neither shift is decisive and the pair does not become solvable.
justification: The two questions are not independent — they share one small world and each option set tells the other what kind of winter this was — but the coupling is weaker than in las-b22-002 because it lives in the options rather than in a stem, and because both questions remain genuinely unresolved. What I could infer as a pair: that this is a cold-season haul over ice with horses, organised around trips, and that the ice's condition is the story's constraint. What I could not: whether the hooves broke through, slipped, or were studded, and whether the organising fact is turn-taking between households or the impossibility of scheduling.
